::: {.hero}
# the etverse {.hero-title}

An R ecosystem for **triangulating causal evidence** in epidemiology.

No single study design or analytic method is free of bias. The etverse gives
each approach its own focused package, with a shared grammar, so that you can
estimate the same effect several different ways — and trust it more when the
answers converge.

[Read the philosophy →](philosophy.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg role="button"}
[Browse on GitHub](https://github.com/etverse){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-lg role="button"}
:::

## Why triangulate? {.mt-5}

Triangulation integrates results from approaches with **different and unrelated
sources of potential bias**. When estimates from methods that would fail in
different ways still point to the same answer, confidence in that answer grows.
The etverse builds this idea into tooling across three levels:

::: {.grid .level-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Methodological
The same estimand, estimated several ways — g-computation, IPW, AIPW,
g-estimation, matching — each leaning on different modelling assumptions.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Design
The same question, asked through different study designs — cohort, case-control,
target-trial emulation, negative controls — each vulnerable to different biases.
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### Evidence
Findings integrated across data sources, populations, and assumptions, rather
than resting on a single point estimate from a single dataset.
:::
:::

## Packages {#packages .mt-5}

Every package ends in `-tr` — for *triangulation*. Each does one job well and
composes with the others through a shared engine.

::: {.grid .pkg-grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### [causatr](https://etverse.github.io/causatr/) [available]{.badge .bg-success}
Causal effects of point treatments: g-computation, inverse-probability weighting, doubly-robust AIPW, structural nested mean models and matching. The engine the rest of the etverse builds on.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### dynamatr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
Causal effects of time-varying treatments: ICE g-computation, natural-history modified treatment policies, and longitudinal IPW, AIPW and structural nested models.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### [survatr](https://etverse.github.io/survatr/) [available]{.badge .bg-success}
Causal survival analysis on person-period data: pooled-logistic hazard
g-computation, IPW and ICE for time-to-event outcomes, risk-difference / RMST
contrasts, competing risks, and IPCW.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### [matchatr](https://etverse.github.io/matchatr/) [in development]{.badge .bg-warning .text-dark}
Classical and causal estimation for (matched) case-control, nested case-control,
and case-cohort designs — conditional logistic and weighted Cox models, plus
case-control–weighted marginal effects that compose with causatr and survatr.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### [negatr](https://etverse.github.io/negatr/) [in development]{.badge .bg-warning .text-dark}
Negative-control methods for detecting and correcting unmeasured confounding,
selection bias, and measurement error — from simple null tests to proximal
causal inference and empirical calibration.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### biasetr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
Quantitative bias analysis — modelling how much a finding could shift under
plausible biases, for the general case not covered by the negative-control
machinery in negatr.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### separatr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
Separable effects — decomposing a treatment effect into components acting
through distinct mechanisms, for sharper, more mechanistic causal questions.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### dagtr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
Directed acyclic graphs for encoding causal assumptions and deriving adjustment
sets to drive the estimators above.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### emulatr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
Target-trial emulation — turning an observational question into an explicit
protocol and analysis.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .pkg-card}
### triangulatr [planned]{.badge .bg-secondary}
The meta-package — collect estimates from across the etverse and assess whether
they triangulate.
:::

:::

::: {.callout-note}
The etverse is early and evolving. Package scopes marked *planned* describe
intended direction and may change.
:::
